why:
Advances BL-20260807-EXIT-ANCHOR-VALIDATED-ON-DISJOINT-POPULATION (open 36 days) by MEASURING the disjointness it argues structurally, and fixes a SECOND defect found underneath it. Tier-1: scripts/research/**, tests/**, docs/claude/**. No src/, no order path — the validators are offline research scripts.

THE DISJOINTNESS, NOW WITH A DENOMINATOR. Population: the newest 1000 `trades` rows via /api/diag/journal, 2026-09-12 (positive control /api/health -> 200). `exit_price_source`: (none) 484 · candle_at_close 355 · exchange_fill 93 · bybit_closed_pnl 28 · recorded_exit_price 17 · verdict 13 · exchange 5 · ib_execution 5. The anchor's APPLIED population is 355; the validated population under the canonical ground-truth set is 131; the OVERLAP IS ZERO BY CONSTRUCTION, since a row carries exactly one exit_price_source. The row's claim holds and is no longer only an argument.

⚠️ THE SECOND DEFECT, WHICH THE ROW DID NOT KNOW ABOUT AND IS WORSE. Both validators carried a LOCAL copy of 'which sources are broker truth' while src/runtime/provenance.py is the declared single owner of exactly that question — CLAUDE.md: 'One module owns this ... Import it; do not re-derive the vocabulary.' The copy had drifted in BOTH directions. Over the same 1000 rows: the validators' set matched 50, provenance.MEASURED_SOURCES matches 131, only 33 in both.
  · ONLY the validators (17): `recorded_exit_price`, DEMOTED from MEASURED on 2026-08-24 by an operator-approved change because it is not a fill. It buckets `estimated` — THE SAME BUCKET AS `candle_at_close`, the estimator under test — so a THIRD of the 'ground truth' was the estimator's own class and the validator was partly grading it against itself. Asserted by RUNNING provenance.classify, not by reading about it.
  · ONLY the canonical set (98): `exchange_fill` 93 + `ib_execution` 5 — the validators discarded 75% of the broker truth available to them, including the largest genuine source in the journal.

⚠️ AND THE DOCSTRING ALREADY NAMED THE RIGHT OWNER ('exit_price_source in MEASURED_SOURCES') while the code named a different set — prose right, field wrong, which is the direction 'field beats comment' does not cover and is why the drift was invisible to a reader.

SHIPPED: both validators import provenance.MEASURED_SOURCES and REFUSE to run if the import fails rather than falling back to a local copy — a fallback set is the second definition again, and silent. tests/test_exit_reconstruction_ground_truth.py grades the CODE rather than the prose (AST, so a docstring naming the set is fine) and pins both directions; MUTATION-TESTED — restoring a local set makes it fail, 4 pass clean.

⚠️ THE ROW STAYS OPEN AND ITS SECOND HALF IS RE-STATED, because it was UNSATISFIABLE AS WRITTEN. Half 1 (provenance distinguishes close-time from detection-time anchoring) is src/runtime/ and is TIER-2 by path — a proposal for the manager, not this lane's to land. Half 2 ('the accuracy figure is computed on the population it is applied to') cannot be done directly and no amount of re-validation will achieve it: the applied population is DEFINED by having no broker price, so it has no ground truth to compare against. The criterion now names the achievable substitute — rows that DO carry broker truth AND share the applied population's defining property, a `closed_at` that is a DETECTION time rather than a fill time — with the honest fallback stated: if no such rows exist, the estimator's accuracy on its applied population is UNMEASURABLE and must be said so beside every figure derived from it. That is a defensible close and far better than a number quoted from a disjoint population.

⚠️ AND ANY FIGURE FROM A RUN BEFORE THIS FIX IS ON THE WRONG DENOMINATOR and must not be re-used — recorded on the criterion so the '1.33 bps' the row quotes is not carried forward by accident.
